info.title: Lab Sample Pickup and Delivery API
info.description: Role-aware API for configuring the clinical logistics network as one unified location model, checking serviceability without creating anything, planning and revalidating sample journeys, executing custody-safe handoffs, recovering from disruptions, and querying live operational state and the immutable audit trail. Every response is wrapped as {"data": ...}; every failure is {"error": ..., "code": ...}. Authorization always follows the role the session has SELECTED, never the union of roles the account holds.

post.description: Accepts work that was offered to the caller. Work is offered to one eligible worker at a time, and only the offered worker may accept: work that has not been offered to anybody yet is refused with 409 offer_not_offered, and work offered to somebody else with 409 offer_not_available. Roles: collection_professional, delivery_partner, node_handler, laboratory_team. A multi-role account must select the role it is acting under first; until it does, this operation is refused with 409 role_not_selected.

post.description: DRY RUN of the serviceability decision. It answers exactly the question create_collection_request answers, using the same shared decision, WITHOUT creating anything: no collection request, sample, journey, assignment, stop, capacity reservation, handoff, idempotency record, worker fairness counter or audit event, and it never consumes an idempotency key. A request is serviceable only when the origin is within the inclusive 5 km coverage of an active collection point, an active laboratory accepts the sample type, a valid route exists, regular and cooled capacity are available, handling and container rules are satisfiable, and arrival beats the deadline. The verdict reads only network structure, never any worker's availability. Roles: requester, dispatcher, administrator. A multi-role account must select the role it is acting under first; until it does, this operation is refused with 409 role_not_selected.

Cooled capacity is a subset of total capacity and neither dimension may be reduced below what is already reserved. Roles: administrator, node_handler, laboratory_team. post.description: Confirms one side of a pending custody transfer. Both the sender and the receiver must confirm: a one-sided confirmation does not transfer custody and the sender stays responsible. Custody flips to the receiver exactly when the handoff completes, and repeated or delayed confirmations cannot create a second transfer. Only the named sender or receiver may confirm. Role-independent: it is authorized by the caller's part in the handoff.

post.description: Creates a sample type with its container, temperature range, collector qualification, incompatibilities, cooled-route requirement and batching policy. The named profiles carry non-configurable safety policy in addition to the generic attributes: Amber requires LX-A, Indigo requires LX-I and is automatically made symmetrically incompatible with Amber, Frost requires LX-F plus a cooled route and a cooling-capable container, and Pulse requires LX-P and may never be batched. Roles: administrator. A multi-role account must select the role it is acting under first; until it does, this operation is refused with 409 role_not_selected.

post.description: Applies one change to an active journey plan: add_stop, remove_stop, reorder_stops, replace_worker or reassign_worker, merge_samples, split_samples or split_batch, cancel_work, reroute or replace_route. Any other changeType is refused with 400 invalid_change_type. The WHOLE candidate plan is revalidated — every affected leg, stop order, worker eligibility, compatibility, capacity reservation and deadline — and if any clause fails the change is rejected and the current plan is kept unchanged, because the whole compare-and-swap transaction is rolled back. Every branch answers with the whole journey plan; a reroute or replace_route also carries replanStatus and, when one was built, the replacement plan. Swapping a worker on planned work is audited as an override. Roles: dispatcher, administrator. A multi-role account must select the role it is acting under first; until it does, this operation is refused with 409 role_not_selected.

post.description: Searches the immutable audit trail. Records are returned NEWEST FIRST by default and the response reports total, hasMore and nextOffset, so recent history stays reachable on a long-lived instance whose trail has grown far past one page, and every older record is still reachable by paging with offset. Pinning both entityType and entityId makes the search an entity trace: the whole chain for that request, sample, journey, assignment, handoff or account is returned in one call rather than a page of the global trail. Filters compose: actorId, entityType, entityId, action, role, success, fromTime, toTime and a free-text query over the action and the recorded changes. Roles: administrator, dispatcher. A multi-role account must select the role it is acting under first; until it does, this operation is refused with 409 role_not_selected.

success.description: Outcome. A refused or failed action is recorded as false.
